instruction: Please implement a supply chain traceability website for tracking and verifying the origin and circulation of products with the unique product IDs. The website should have functionalities for product registration, tracking, inquiry, and verification. Users should be able to register products, track the circulation path of products, query the current status of products, and verify the authenticity of products. The website should also have data statistics and analysis functions to help users understand the operation of the supply chain. Define the background as misty rose and components as firebrick.

ui_instruct.task: Test the product registration form by entering valid product details and submitting the form.
ui_instruct.expected_result: The product is successfully registered in the system, and a confirmation message is displayed with a unique product ID.

ui_instruct.task: Navigate to the product tracking page and enter the unique product ID to track its circulation path.
ui_instruct.expected_result: The circulation path of the product appears, detailing each location or checkpoint the product has passed through up to the present.

ui_instruct.task: On the website, use the product inquiry feature to check the current status of an already registered product using its ID.
ui_instruct.expected_result: The current status of the product is correctly displayed, including relevant details such as location and time.

ui_instruct.task: Verify the authenticity of a product by entering its ID in the verification section.
ui_instruct.expected_result: The website confirms the authenticity of the product and provides the source information as registered.

ui_instruct.task: Access the data statistics and analysis page and review the displayed metrics.
ui_instruct.expected_result: The page displays relevant and comprehensive statistics and analysis regarding supply chain operations, such as total products tracked and current circulation statuses.

ui_instruct.task: Check the navigation menu across different pages to ensure consistent access to main functionalities (registration, tracking, inquiry, verification, statistics).
ui_instruct.expected_result: All main functionalities are easily accessible from the navigation menu, and links correctly route to respective pages.

ui_instruct.task: Verify that the website uses 'misty rose' as the background color and 'firebrick' as the component color, as specified in the design requirements.
ui_instruct.expected_result: The website has a background color of 'misty rose' and components (such as buttons, cards, headers, etc.) are styled with the color 'firebrick', accurately reflecting the design instruction.

follow_ups.instruction: The registry's working, so let's do lot-level grouping next. I want a Lots page where products sit under a shared lot number - each lot card lists its members with a member count and a rolled-up lot status (a single flagged product makes the whole lot Flagged, otherwise anything still moving makes it In Transit, and only an all-delivered lot reads Delivered), and the cards order themselves by whichever lot had journey activity most recently, newest on top; also put a lot picker on the registration form so new products can join an existing lot. Seed it with exactly these seven products in three lots - I'll grow it later: LOT-COF-01 has PT-1001 Arabica Beans 5kg from Bogota (Registered at Bogota Farm Mar 2 2026, Shipped from Bogota Port Mar 5, Arrived Rotterdam Port Mar 12, Customs cleared Rotterdam Port Mar 14 - currently In Transit), PT-1002 Arabica Beans 10kg from Bogota (Registered Bogota Farm Mar 2, Shipped Bogota Port Mar 6, Delivered Berlin Warehouse Mar 20 - Delivered), and PT-1003 Robusta Blend from Hanoi (Registered Hanoi Facility Mar 8, Quality check Hanoi Facility Mar 8, Flagged Hanoi Facility Mar 9 - Flagged); LOT-TEA-02 has PT-1004 Ceylon Black Tea from Colombo (Registered Colombo Estate Apr 1, Shipped Colombo Port Apr 3, Arrived Rotterdam Port Apr 10 - In Transit) and PT-1005 Green Tea Sencha from Shizuoka (Registered Shizuoka Farm Apr 2, Delivered Osaka Depot Apr 15 - Delivered); LOT-CAC-03 has PT-1006 Cacao Nibs from Accra (Registered Accra Co-op Feb 10, Shipped Tema Port Feb 14, Delivered Antwerp Hub Feb 28 - Delivered) and PT-1007 Cacao Butter from Accra (Registered Accra Co-op Feb 10, Delivered Antwerp Hub Mar 1 - Delivered). Two things I want everywhere in this app, now and for anything we add later: product IDs always shown in that PT-#### style, and statuses always as little colored pills - green for Delivered, amber for In Transit, red for Flagged or Recalled.

ui_instruct.task: Open the Lots page on a freshly loaded app and read the order of the lot cards from top to bottom.
ui_instruct.expected_result: Exactly three lot cards appear ordered LOT-TEA-02, then LOT-COF-01, then LOT-CAC-03 - most recent journey activity first (Apr 15, Mar 20, Mar 1 2026 respectively), not alphabetical order and not the order the lots were entered.

ui_instruct.expected_result: LOT-COF-01 shows 3 member products and its rolled-up status reads Flagged with a red status pill - one flagged member (PT-1003) makes the whole lot Flagged even though its other two members are In Transit and Delivered.

ui_instruct.task: Open the Lots page and find the LOT-TEA-02 card.
ui_instruct.expected_result: It shows 2 members and its rolled-up status reads In Transit with an amber pill - PT-1005 being Delivered doesn't make the lot Delivered while PT-1004 is still moving.

ui_instruct.task: Use the registration form to register a product named Oolong Reserve, choosing LOT-TEA-02 in the lot picker (fill any other required fields with valid entries), then open the Lots page.
ui_instruct.expected_result: The LOT-TEA-02 card now lists 3 member products including Oolong Reserve.

ui_instruct.expected_result: A confirmation appears showing the product was registered along with a unique product ID assigned to it.

follow_ups.instruction: Partners send me event data as spreadsheets, so I need a bulk importer: a big paste box where each line reads product ID, event type, location, date - like PT-1004, Arrived, Hamburg Hub, 2026-04-20 - with event types limited to Shipped, Arrived, Delivered and Flagged. Validate line by line as I type or paste: a running tally of valid versus invalid lines, and each bad line labeled with why (unknown product ID, bad event type, date not YYYY-MM-DD, or a date earlier than that product's latest journey event). The import button commits only the valid lines and reports how many landed; committed events go straight onto each product's journey, updating its current status and location to the newest event - and if that flips a product to Flagged, its lot card should flip with it. One more house style while we're at it: everywhere a date shows up in this app, now and in whatever we build later, write it like Apr 20, 2026 - never numeric slashes.
follow_ups.source_feature: ERP / WMS Integration via API (CSV bulk-import of events)

ui_instruct.expected_result: Before importing the tally reads 1 valid and 1 invalid (the second line labeled with an unknown-product reason for PT-9999), and the import summary reports exactly 1 event added - PT-1004's journey gains the Hamburg Hub arrival while nothing is created for PT-9999.

ui_instruct.task: Paste the single line 'PT-1004, Delivered, Hamburg Hub, 2026-04-05' into the bulk importer's paste box.
ui_instruct.expected_result: The line is marked invalid with a reason saying the date is earlier than PT-1004's latest journey event (its Rotterdam Port arrival on Apr 10, 2026), the running tally shows 0 valid and 1 invalid, and importing commits nothing.

ui_instruct.task: Type the single line 'PT-1005, Shipped, Osaka Depot, 2026-04-18' into the paste box and watch the tally, then edit the word Shipped to Teleported.
ui_instruct.expected_result: While the line is intact the tally shows 1 valid and 0 invalid; as soon as the event type becomes Teleported the line flips to invalid with a bad-event-type reason and the tally updates to 0 valid and 1 invalid - all without pressing import.

ui_instruct.task: Paste 'PT-1005, Flagged, Osaka Depot, 2026-04-20' into the importer, press import, then open the Lots page.
ui_instruct.expected_result: PT-1005 now shows status Flagged, and the LOT-TEA-02 card's rolled-up status flips to Flagged with a red pill (it was In Transit before the import).

ui_instruct.task: Open the Lots page and find the LOT-COF-01 card.
ui_instruct.expected_result: LOT-COF-01 shows 3 member products and its rolled-up status reads Flagged with a red status pill - one flagged member (PT-1003) makes the whole lot Flagged even though its other two members are In Transit and Delivered.

follow_ups.instruction: Counterfeiters test-scan stolen codes in bursts, so let's catch that: log every authenticity check run in the verification section, and give me a Scan Monitor page where every product has a row listing its scan dates, a total scan count, and a suspicious flag. Suspicion works off a threshold box (start it at 2) - a product gets flagged when it's been checked more than that many times inside any single 7-day stretch; it's the burst that matters, not the lifetime total, and the list should re-evaluate the moment I change the number. Backfill the log with this history: PT-1001 scanned Mar 1, Apr 1 and May 1 2026; PT-1003 scanned Mar 9, Mar 10, Mar 10, Mar 11 and Apr 20; PT-1004 scanned Apr 12; PT-1005 scanned Apr 16 and Apr 17; PT-1006 scanned Feb 20, Feb 21 and Feb 22.
follow_ups.source_feature: Geo-Location Counterfeit Detection (fused with per-product verification history log)

ui_instruct.task: Open the Scan Monitor with the threshold box at its default of 2 and check which products carry the suspicious flag.
ui_instruct.expected_result: Exactly PT-1003 and PT-1006 are flagged suspicious (4 scans within Mar 9-11 and 3 scans within Feb 20-22 respectively); PT-1001 is NOT flagged even though it has 3 lifetime scans, because they are spread a month apart - no 7-day stretch holds more than 2.

ui_instruct.task: On the Scan Monitor, change the threshold box value to 3.
ui_instruct.expected_result: The list re-evaluates immediately: PT-1006 loses its suspicious flag (its densest 7-day stretch is exactly 3 scans, not more than 3) while PT-1003 stays flagged (4 scans between Mar 9 and Mar 11, 2026).

ui_instruct.task: Scroll the Scan Monitor to the rows for PT-1002 and PT-1007.
ui_instruct.expected_result: Both appear as normal rows with 0 total scans and no suspicious flag - never-scanned products still render and the page doesn't blank or error.

ui_instruct.task: Run an authenticity check on PT-1004 in the verification section, then open the Scan Monitor and find PT-1004's row.
ui_instruct.expected_result: Its total scan count reads 2 - the seeded Apr 12, 2026 scan plus the check just performed - showing live verification checks land in the log.

ui_instruct.task: Paste the single line 'PT-1004, Delivered, Hamburg Hub, 2026-04-05' into the bulk importer's paste box.
ui_instruct.expected_result: The line is marked invalid with a reason saying the date is earlier than PT-1004's latest journey event (its Rotterdam Port arrival on Apr 10, 2026), the running tally shows 0 valid and 1 invalid, and importing commits nothing.

follow_ups.instruction: Next up: recalls. From any lot I want to kick off a recall - first a review screen that lists every member product with its current status and the total affected count, and nothing actually changes until I hit confirm; then every member flips to Recalled across the whole app. Confirmed recalls live on a Recalls page with progress shown like 1 of 3 retrieved - I tick members off as units come back, and the instant the last one is ticked the recall closes itself out as Completed (the products stay Recalled though; retrieved just means we physically got the unit back).
follow_ups.source_feature: Lot-Level Batch Tracking (recall scoped to a production lot)

ui_instruct.task: Start a recall on LOT-COF-01 and stop at the review screen without confirming.
ui_instruct.expected_result: The review lists exactly 3 affected products - PT-1001, PT-1002 and PT-1003 with their current statuses - and states 3 as the total affected count, and no product status changes while the recall is unconfirmed.

ui_instruct.task: Start a recall on LOT-CAC-03, confirm it on the review screen, then look at PT-1006 and PT-1007 wherever they are listed.
ui_instruct.expected_result: Both products flip to Recalled with red pills, and the Recalls page shows the recall live with progress 0 of 2 retrieved.

ui_instruct.task: Start a recall on LOT-CAC-03, confirm it on the review screen, then mark PT-1006 as retrieved and then PT-1007 as retrieved.
ui_instruct.expected_result: After the first tick the recall shows 1 of 2 retrieved and stays open; the moment PT-1007 is ticked it reads 2 of 2 and the recall automatically closes as Completed, while both products still show status Recalled.

ui_instruct.task: Start and confirm a recall on LOT-CAC-03, then use the product inquiry to look up PT-1007.
ui_instruct.expected_result: The inquiry reports PT-1007's current status as Recalled with a red pill, consistent with the recall just confirmed.

ui_instruct.task: Open the Lots page on a freshly loaded app and read the order of the lot cards from top to bottom.
ui_instruct.expected_result: Exactly three lot cards appear ordered LOT-TEA-02, then LOT-COF-01, then LOT-CAC-03 - most recent journey activity first (Apr 15, Mar 20, Mar 1 2026 respectively), not alphabetical order and not the order the lots were entered.

follow_ups.instruction: Something that's been biting us: partner data leaves holes in the custody chain, so I want a Chain Audit page that sweeps every product's journey in the registry and surfaces the gaps. Two things count as an issue: a Delivered event with no Shipped event anywhere before it (the shipping leg got skipped), and any event dated after a product was already Delivered (activity after delivery). Each issue entry names the product, says which rule it broke, and cites the offending event with its location and date. Arrange the whole page by lot: lots carrying issues float to the top ordered by how many issues they hold, alphabetical by lot number on ties, and clean lots sit underneath with a clean badge. It has to stay honest as data flows in - anything the bulk importer commits gets re-audited the moment it lands. And to be clear, a product sitting at Flagged is not by itself an audit issue: flags are a status problem, custody gaps are a data problem.
follow_ups.source_feature: First Mile Traceability data integrity (custody-chain gap auditing across event journeys)

follow_ups.instruction: The single-ID inquiry doesn't cut it for portfolio questions - build me a Screener page over the whole registry. A search box that narrows by name or ID as I type, status checkboxes where ticking several means any of them counts (Delivered plus In Transit shows both), and lot and origin pickers that stack on as and-conditions; keep a live count like 2 of 7 products pinned to the results. Let me save the current filter combo as a named preset and bring it back with one click, give me a copy-ready text export of exactly what's matching rendered on the page, and when nothing matches show a clear no-products-match note instead of an empty void.
follow_ups.source_feature: Real-Time Analytics Dashboard (drill-down filtering adapted into a registry screener)

follow_ups.instruction: Field teams keep finding knock-offs, so add a counterfeit reporting flow. A report form - product ID, where it was found, what looks off - that refuses to submit while anything's empty and rejects IDs that aren't in our registry with a clear not-recognized message right on the form. Reports land as Open in an Investigations queue; opening one shows the report side by side with that product's verification scan history from the monitor as evidence, and I close it either as Genuine (product untouched) or Counterfeit Confirmed, which flips the product to Flagged everywhere, its lot card included. Seed the queue with two open ones: R-01 filed Apr 18, 2026 against PT-1005, found at a Lisbon street market, 'hologram sticker missing'; and R-02 filed Apr 21, 2026 against PT-1002, found in an online listing, 'suspiciously cheap'.
follow_ups.source_feature: Geo-Location Counterfeit Detection (extended into a report intake and investigation queue)

ui_instruct.expected_result: PT-1005 flips to Flagged, and LOT-TEA-02's rolled-up status now reads Flagged with a red pill (it read In Transit before).

follow_ups.instruction: Last big piece: a Checkpoints page rolling up every journey event in the registry by location. Each location gets a row with how many distinct products passed through it, the total event count there, and the latest activity date - ranked most distinct products first, alphabetical when they tie, and a product that hits the same checkpoint twice still counts once. Anything that lands in a journey through the bulk importer should flow in here too, brand-new locations included.
follow_ups.source_feature: Supply Chain Timeline / Event Map (aggregated across products into checkpoint analytics)

target_app_summary: The base traceability site (register products, track circulation, inquire status, verify authenticity, view stats) grows into a full supply-chain integrity platform. Operations gains lot-level grouping with rolled-up lot statuses, a validating bulk event importer that feeds product journeys, and a lot-scoped recall workflow with retrieval progress and auto-close. Anti-counterfeit tooling adds a scan monitor that logs every verification check and flags 7-day scan bursts against a typed threshold, plus a counterfeit report intake and investigation queue that uses the scan log as evidence and can flip products (and their lots) to Flagged. Discovery and quality surfaces add a multi-criteria registry screener with any-of status logic, presets and an on-page text export, a chain integrity audit that sweeps every journey for custody gaps (skipped shipping legs, activity after delivery) and ranks lots by issue count with clean badges, and a checkpoint analytics page that dedups products per location and ranks with alphabetical tie-breaks. A mid-ladder restyle unifies five surfaces under one firebrick-on-misty-rose skin. The graph runs deep: lots feed recalls and every lot-grouped rollup, and the importer feeds lot rollups, the integrity audit, and checkpoint analytics.
